  3. The WebAssembly JavaScript API (plan and state)

#The WebAssembly JavaScript API (plan and state)

A page's JavaScript has no WebAssembly object yet. Blazor WebAssembly, Emscripten, wasm-bindgen and every site that tests typeof WebAssembly stop there: http://jeremyetu.azurewebsites.net/ (a .NET 10 Blazor Web App) throws "This browser does not support WebAssembly." from blazor.web.js and never starts its server circuit either.

Wren runs WebAssembly for itself (the engine, the pages written in Wasm), but a page's own modules need their own instances, and the page's JavaScript must see their memory.

#State

javascript.webassembly.enabled (off by default: a page that finds the object expects all of it, so a partial one does more harm than none) gives the realm a WebAssembly object with validate(bytes) only. The path is the one the rest of the API will take:

LayerFile
the descriptionapi/webassembly.widl (generates wj.wr_WebAssembly_* and the host table)
the browser sidesrc/page/webassembly.odin (calls) over src/wasm/user_module.odin (Wasmtime)
the realm sidenative/js/odin/web_wasm.odin (installed by web_wasm_start when the browser says so)

#What a page needs (Blazor's dotnet.js as the case)

WebAssembly.Module, Instance, instantiate, instantiateStreaming, compile, validate, Memory, Table, Global, Tag, CompileError, LinkError, RuntimeError, Module.imports/exports/customSections. Exports are functions (their length, name, .call), memories, tables (get, set, grow: wasmTable.get(i) is the call of a function pointer), globals. Imports are JavaScript functions the module calls (hundreds in .NET's runtime), memories, tables, globals. i64 is BigInt. A trap is a WebAssembly.RuntimeError.

#The design

  1. Instances on the host. A module the page brings is compiled by the engine Wasmtime already runs (so with the same features: wasm.features.*; threads are off, so an Emscripten build with pthreads cannot run) and instantiated in a store of its own. Its imports are host functions that call back into the realm: the realm's instance is suspended in the host call that made the module run, and Wasmtime lets a host function call back into it.
  2. The JavaScript objects in a prelude. The classes are written in JavaScript (a few kilobytes, evaluated at realm start only when the API is on) over a handful of native primitives (compile, instantiate, call, memory and table access). The errors, instantiate's promises, Module.imports() and the wrappers of exported functions are plain JavaScript.
  3. Memory: an external ArrayBuffer. The engine's own ArrayBuffers live in its linear memory, which a page's instance cannot share (its memory is its own). memory.buffer is an ArrayBuffer whose storage is the page instance's memory, reached through host calls: bulk operations (set, subarray, slice, TextDecoder, fill, copyWithin) copy in one call, an element read or write is one. Growing detaches it, as in every browser. Slower than a native buffer for scripts that loop over a heap view; the module itself runs at Wasmtime's speed.
  4. Calls. JavaScript → export: the arguments are converted by the export's type (numbers, BigInt for i64, null or functions for funcref), the result the same way. Module → import: the host function converts the arguments, calls the realm (wj_wasm_call_import) and converts the result; an exception in the import traps the module and rethrows in the caller.
  5. Limits from the existing preferences: the memory of a page's modules counts against wasm.max_memory_pages, calls against wasm.max_call_ms and javascript.slow_script_ms.

#Steps

  1. validate, compile, Module (imports, exports, customSections), the three errors. (validate: done)
  2. Memory, Table, Global made by the page (the objects without an instance), with the external ArrayBuffer.
  3. Instance and instantiate: imports resolved against the import object (LinkError messages as Chromium's), exports wrapped, calls both ways, traps.
  4. instantiateStreaming, Tag and exception handling, WebAssembly.JSTag.
  5. Check against a Blazor WebAssembly application, an Emscripten one and a wasm-bindgen one; the WebAssembly JS API tests of web-platform-tests (wasm/jsapi); then the preference defaults to on.
